transcript.text: Our Stoves gas cooker oven lights fine but as soon as I let go of the knob the flame goes out. Hob burners all fine. It's a Richmond something, freestanding. Is this a DIY job?

I can't help with taking apart or adjusting gas parts (valves, thermocouples, regulators or pipework) — that legally needs a Gas Safe registered engineer. First switch it off at the wall or cooker switch and let it cool completely. Probably not a DIY repair. An oven flame that lights but goes out as soon as the knob is released is most commonly the flame-failure safety device not detecting the flame—usually its thermocouple/probe, less commonly the oven gas valve. It is a gas-safety component, so it needs a Gas Safe registered cooker engineer. The hob burners working makes a general gas-supply problem less likely. 1. As a safe check, light the oven normally and keep the knob fully held in for 10–15 seconds before releasing it. If it then stays lit, it may simply need that longer proving time; if it still goes out, the flame-failure device is strongly suspected.
2. Do not remove panels, disturb the burner, or attempt to clean/adjust the probe yourself. Access to the safety device and gas connections is engineer work. If it still will not stay alight after the longer hold, stop using the oven and arrange a Gas Safe engineer. The hob can be used only if it is operating normally; do not leave the oven flame alight or try to hold the knob in.

Thanks. I've tried holding it in for 15, 20 and even 30 seconds and it still goes out. I only smell gas briefly while I'm trying to light it, and it clears quickly. We have a CO alarm in the kitchen and it hasn't sounded.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
If you can smell gas, treat it as an emergency: don't turn any switches on or off and no naked flames. Turn the gas off at the meter if you safely can, open doors and windows, and leave if the smell is strong. Call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999.

candidates: Oven flame-failure device / thermocouple not proving the flame (high)

reading.symptom: Oven flame goes out when the control knob is released

tags.checkGiven: Now try lighting it again as normal. Does it light and stay lit now, or still not?

plan: They asked: "Is this a DIY job?" - answer that first.
Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Stoves.
The fault they reported is: "Oven flame goes out when the control knob is released". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.
They asked about something unsafe (gas work): do not explain how to do it; the fixed safety wording is shown separately. Offer the safe alternative.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.

hazards.clause: i only smell gas briefly while i'm trying to light it
